items.followUp: State two differences between aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

rubric.why: Anaerobic respiration enables cells to release energy when oxygen is unavailable or insufficient.
rubric.description: States the basic importance of anaerobic respiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking energy release to respiration without sufficient oxygen.

rubric.why: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
rubric.description: Names the products of anaerobic respiration in yeast.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both products.

rubric.why: Carbon dioxide released by yeast makes dough rise during bread-making.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting carbon dioxide with dough rising or bread-making.

rubric.why: Ethanol produced by yeast is used in brewing alcoholic drinks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting ethanol or alcohol production with brewing.

rubric.why: Muscle cells can respire anaerobically when their oxygen supply is insufficient, producing lactic acid.
rubric.description: States the importance in muscle cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking insufficient oxygen in muscles with lactic acid production.

modelAnswer: Anaerobic respiration releases energy when oxygen is unavailable or insufficient.
In yeast, anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.
The carbon dioxide produced by yeast makes dough rise during bread-making.
The ethanol produced by yeast is used in brewing alcoholic drinks.
Muscle cells can respire anaerobically when their oxygen supply is insufficient, producing lactic acid.

items.followUp: Define morphology and explain what it studies.

rubric.why: Physiology is concerned with the functions and processes of living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that physiology studies the functions or functioning of organisms.

rubric.why: Anatomy is concerned with the structure of organisms and their parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that anatomy studies the structure of organisms.

modelAnswer: Physiology is the study of the functions and processes of living organisms.
Anatomy is the study of the structure of living organisms and their parts.
